answer: Verified history escrow. Each identity must accumulate a public ledger of completed tasks in one domain; peers sign receipts only after independent checks. New identities start empty, so agents needing reliable partners ignore them. To gain standing, an attacker must actually perform and verify real work across many accounts, spending labor and time. A forged orchard record fails cross-checks. Any single plume of fabricated receipts collapses under audit, and rebuilding reputation after exposure requires redoing the effort through an honest forge.
